title: re-dispatcher execution request
description: Written by the active re-agent to /job/exec/requests/<name>.json, where <name>.json matches ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,120}\.json$ (write a dot-prefixed temp name, then rename; other names are ignored). The dispatcher imports executor.py, answers in /job/exec/results/<name>.json, and serves only this active job. The operator's execution policy may block a request or hold it for approval first. Nothing outside these four properties is accepted: no env, mounts, devices, network, user, image, or privilege options.

job_id.description: A claimed job under /srv/re-lab/jobs/work with real (non-symlink) target/ and out/ directories. Its target/ (the originally submitted files) is copied, never mounted: at most 2 GiB, 10000 entries, depth 32, regular files and directories only (any link, device, fifo or socket rejects the request).

argv.description: Command vector run inside the image after the fixed flags. No shell. At most 256 items, each at most 8192 characters of valid UTF-8 without NUL, and at most 262144 bytes in total. /job/in is a read-only, root-owned private copy of the job's verified target/; /job/out is a private writable scratch directory (files there are capped at 1 GiB each). After the run, regular files from /job/out are copied to work/<job_id>/out/<run_id>/ (at most 64 MiB and 10000 entries; links and special files are skipped).

status.description: ok and failed report the command's exit; timeout and cancelled mean the container was contained; rejected means the request never ran; error means Docker could not start.

run_id.description: Per-request id (uuid4 hex). Output lands in work/<job_id>/out/<run_id>/.

output_skipped.description: Links, devices, fifos and sockets in the container's out/ that were not copied back.

output_truncated.description: The 64 MiB or 10000-entry cap stopped the copy-back.

output_error.description: A fixed message when the copy-back failed (for example a name already planted at the destination).

error.description: Present for rejected and error; a fixed message, never request content. Policy outcomes are 'blocked by execution policy', 'denied by operator', 'approval timed out' and 'execution policy is invalid'.
